study_notes.topic: Classification or Odd One Out (Verbal Reasoning)

sections.title: Basic Concept of Classification
sections.content: In Classification or Odd One Out questions, four options are given in which three share a common property while one is different. Step 1: Read all the options carefully. Step 2: Identify the common property among them. Step 3: The option that does not fit that property will be the Odd One Out.

sections.title: Word Classification
sections.content: Step 1: Understand the meaning of each word. Step 2: Identify their category such as fruits, states, cities, etc. Step 3: Check which word belongs to a different category. Step 4: Select that word as the Odd One Out. Example: Mango, Apple, Banana, Carrot. Here Carrot is different because the other three are fruits.

sections.title: Number Classification
sections.content: Step 1: Observe the numbers carefully. Step 2: Check whether they are odd/even, squares, or cubes. Step 3: Identify if any number follows a different pattern. Step 4: The number that does not follow the pattern will be the Odd One Out. Example: 4, 9, 16, 18. Here 18 is different because the others are perfect squares.

sections.title: Letter Classification
sections.content: Step 1: Look at the letters and identify vowels or consonants. Step 2: Check their alphabetical positions (A=1, B=2...). Step 3: Examine the gaps between letters (+1, +2, etc.). Step 4: The letter that does not follow the pattern will be the Odd One Out. Example: B, D, F, G. Here G is different because the others increase by a +2 gap.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Not understanding the correct meaning of words. 2. Assuming a number pattern too quickly. 3. Remembering alphabetical positions incorrectly. 4. Not comparing all options properly.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: The main task in Odd One Out questions is identifying the common property. In words, check the category; in numbers, observe the mathematical pattern; and in letters, examine the alphabetical logic.

tricks.title: Category Check Trick
tricks.explanation: In word questions, first identify the category.
tricks.example: Lion, Tiger, Cow, Elephant → Cow is different because the others are wild animals.

tricks.title: Odd-Even Quick Check
tricks.explanation: In number questions, first check whether numbers are odd or even.

tricks.title: Alphabet Gap Trick
tricks.example: A, C, E, H → H is different because the others follow a +2 gap.

tricks.title: Vowel-Consonant Check
tricks.explanation: Observe the pattern of vowels and consonants.
tricks.example: A, E, I, B → B is different.

tricks.title: Meaning Comparison
tricks.explanation: Compare the meanings of the words.
tricks.example: Rose, Lily, Lotus, Mango → Mango is different.

tricks.title: Multiples Check
tricks.explanation: Check whether all numbers are multiples of a particular number.

tricks.title: Fast Elimination
tricks.explanation: If three options clearly match, quickly identify the fourth as different.
tricks.example: Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, India → India is different.
